\begin{abstract}
We construct the exact finite conditional-disintegration object required by the
vacuum-weight programme.  Normalization, bad-row formation, weighted
partition-ratio identities, and compatible relabeling covariance are proved
without an independence assumption.  The four-channel H1 star kernel is
realized exactly by a normalized table.  A counterexample shows that an
absolutely small bad numerator is useless when the retained-state normalizer
collapses.  The complete nonlinear boundary-uniform $SU(2)$ kernel remains
open.
\end{abstract}

\section{Conditional object}
Let $S$ be a finite retained-state space and $F_s$ a finite conditional fiber.
For $w_s(f)>0$, a next-state map $\tau_s:F_s\to S$, and bad predicate
$b_s:F_s\to\{0,1\}$, set
\[
 Z(s)=\sum_{f\in F_s}w_s(f),\quad
 P(s,t)=\frac1{Z(s)}\sum_{\tau_s(f)=t}w_s(f),\quad
 Q(s,t)=\frac1{Z(s)}\sum_{\substack{\tau_s(f)=t\\b_s(f)=1}}w_s(f).
\]

\begin{theorem}[Normalized pushforward]
$P$ is stochastic and $Q$ is substochastic.  For every $V:S\to[1,\infty)$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:ratio}
 \frac{(QV)(s)}{V(s)}=
 \frac{\sum_{b_s(f)=1}w_s(f)V(\tau_s(f))}{Z(s)V(s)}.
\end{equation}
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}
Sum first over target states and then over fibers.  Positivity gives
$0\leq Q\leq P$, while every fiber occurs exactly once in the sum defining
$P$.
\end{proof}

Compatible bijections of states and fibers transport $w,\tau,b$ and conjugate
$P,Q$.  This is a finite relabeling theorem; physical gauge covariance still
requires the boundary algebra and Haar disintegration.

\section{Exact four-channel realization}
Let $S=\{0,1,2,3,4\}$, with $0$ regular, and set $e=q^2/4$.  At state $0$ use
one good fiber of weight $1-q^2$ returning to $0$ and four bad fibers of
weight $e$ entering states $1,\dots,4$.  At each charged state use one bad
fiber of unit weight returning to $0$.  Then
\[
 Q_{0a}=\frac{q^2}{4},\qquad Q_{a0}=1,qquad
 V=(1,q^{-1},q^{-1},q^{-1},q^{-1}),
\]
and equation~\eqref{eq:ratio} gives $(QV)/V=q$ in every state.  For
\[
 q=0.002430277501841998
\]
the executable identity error is exactly zero in binary floating arithmetic.

\section{Normalizer obstruction}
\begin{proposition}
Absolute suppression of a bad numerator does not imply conditional
suppression.
\end{proposition}
\begin{proof}
Take $Z_G(L)=e^{-2L}$ and $Z_B(L)=e^{-L}$.  Both vanish, but
\[
 \frac{Z_B(L)}{Z_G(L)+Z_B(L)}=\frac1{1+e^{-L}}\longrightarrow1.
\]
At $L=12$, the bad weight is $6.1442\times10^{-6}$ while its normalized
probability is $0.9999938558$.
\end{proof}

\begin{warning}
No action-only estimate may replace the retained-state partition normalizer.
The physical target is a compact nonlinear $SU(2)$ fiber, uniformly over
positive-mass histories, volume, cutoff, charts, center sectors, orbit/cut
data, and integer topology.
\end{warning}

\section{Audit}
The exact finite theorem is C2.  The physical nonlinear kernel, its uniform
normalizer, one-scale basin entry, repeated RG, continuum construction, and a
mass gap are not proved.  Nine hostile regression tests verify normalization,
weighted identities, covariance, invalid-input rejection, and the collapsing
normalizer counterexample.
